$schema_note: Full ground-up specification for the SISKARA application, written for a project that is about to be built from scratch. This file is meant to be read by AI coding assistants (e.g. in VS Code / Claude Code) as the single source of truth before writing any code. Keep it updated whenever a design decision changes.
full_name: Sistem Skrining dan Pemeriksaan Kesehatan Kapal dan Pesawat Udara
client: Balai Besar Kekarantinaan Kesehatan (BBKK) Makassar - Kementerian Kesehatan RI
overview: SISKARA digitizes BBKK's health quarantine inspection process for ships and aircraft. Ship/aircraft crew self-declare their sanitation condition through a mobile form -- filling general data, the full sanitation checklist, and capturing evidence photos/videos -- and BBKK staff review that declaration and give a final approve/reject decision. On approval, an official document is generated automatically: a PHQC for ships, or a generic Berkas Verifikasi for aircraft (aircraft never receive a PHQC). Core design principles: (1) a user's role is always determined server-side and never chosen manually at login; (2) all accounts are permanent (no temporary/guest sessions, no QR-code linking mechanism); (3) checklist structure is template-driven in the database so new transport modes or form revisions never require an app code release; (4) a submission is auto-rejected the instant any checklist item fails, without needing a staff review; only submissions that pass automatic evaluation reach the staff review step; (5) the staff member's approval is a single, final decision -- there is no second approval stage anywhere else in the system.

mobile.state_management: Riverpod or BLoC -- pick one and stay consistent across the codebase
key_packages: camera or image_picker (camera-only capture; gallery picking must be disabled for evidence photos/videos)
flutter_secure_storage (session token only -- never store the signing PIN locally)
firebase-admin (server-side only, used inside API routes)
pdf-lib or puppeteer (PDF generation with stamp + signatures, for both PHQC and Berkas Verifikasi templates)

backend.auth_check: Every route verifies the caller's Firebase ID token server-side and reads their role from custom claims via firebase-admin before executing anything.

repository_structure.rationale: Flutter (Dart) and Next.js (TypeScript) share no code, so plain folders are used instead of a monorepo tool (Turborepo/Nx). CI workflows are path-filtered so each app only rebuilds when its own folder changes.

firebase.description: Centralized Firebase security configuration shared by both apps

roles.summary: Self-declares the full ship sanitation form: general data, the entire checklist, evidence photos/videos for failing items, and reasons for failures. Signs digitally as the declarant.

roles.account_creation: Self-registers in the app, or is created on-site by a staf_bbkk user. Account is permanent either way.
roles.summary: Self-declares the full aircraft sanitation form: general data, the entire checklist, evidence photos/videos for failing items, and reasons for failures. Signs digitally as the declarant.

roles.account_creation: Created by Admin only. Permanent account.
roles.summary: Reviews self-declared submissions that already passed automatic checklist evaluation. Gives the approve / reject / request-revision decision. This decision is FINAL (single-stage) and automatically triggers document generation (PHQC for kapal, Berkas Verifikasi for pesawat). Signs digitally as the verifier.

roles.account_creation: Created by Admin (or a bootstrap super-admin account). Permanent account.
roles.summary: Purely administrative: manages user accounts, manages checklist templates, exports data, views generated documents, and reviews audit logs. Has no approve/reject capability anywhere -- that decision belongs exclusively to staf_bbkk.

auth_model.principle: A user's role is fixed once, at account creation, and stored server-side. The client never presents a role picker at login; the app reads the role automatically right after authentication and routes to the matching UI.
auth_model.role_storage: Firebase Auth custom claims are the source of truth for access control, mirrored into a `users` Firestore document for easy querying/display.
login_flow: User authenticates with Firebase Auth (email/password or phone).
Client reads the ID token's custom claim `role`.
Client fetches the matching `users/{uid}` document for profile data (name, signature_url, etc).

The app automatically opens the screen matching that role: kepala_kapal sees the ship sanitation form, kepala_penerbangan sees the aircraft sanitation form, staf_bbkk sees the review/approval queue, validator_admin sees the web admin dashboard. No manual role selection exists anywhere in either app.
auth_model.account_linking: When a staf_bbkk needs to help a kepala who has no account yet, they can create one on the spot (name, id number, phone) directly from the mobile app -- no QR code or session code is used or required.

digital_signature.storage: Each account has one permanent signature image (signature_url), captured once (drawn or uploaded) during account setup.
digital_signature.confirmation_required: A PIN (or password) confirmation is required every time a signature is applied to a document. This check MUST happen server-side (API route), never only on the client.
digital_signature.legal_validity: This is a stored-image signature for internal BBKK documentation purposes only -- it is not a certified electronic signature. A certified e-signature provider (e.g. PrivyID, VIDA, Digisign, Peruri) can be integrated later if legal force becomes a requirement.
digital_signature.stamp: The institutional stamp is a static image baked into the PDF template; it is not tied to any specific user account.

core_business_flow: 1. kepala_kapal or kepala_penerbangan logs in. The app automatically opens the form matching their role (ship sanitation form, or aircraft sanitation form) -- there is no mode/role picker anywhere in the UI.
2. They fill the 'Data Umum' (general data) section for their vessel or flight.
3. They fill the entire checklist themselves (self-declaration), rendered dynamically from the active checklist_template for their transport mode.

4. For any checklist item whose answer falls into a 'fail' category, the app requires a written reason (alasan) and a real-time photo/video captured from the in-app camera (gallery picking is disabled), with GPS and timestamp attached automatically.
5. They sign digitally as the declarant (PIN confirmation triggers the stored signature image being stamped onto the draft document).

6. On submit, the backend evaluates every checklist answer against the active template's fail rules. If any item fails, the submission status becomes `ditolak_otomatis` immediately -- staf_bbkk does not need to act on this, it only appears to them as an informational field-finding report. If every item passes, status becomes `menunggu_verifikasi_staf`.
7. staf_bbkk opens their review queue, which lists submissions with status `menunggu_verifikasi_staf`: general data, checklist answers, and evidence media are all visible there.
8. staf_bbkk approves, or rejects / requests revision. They sign digitally as the verifier (PIN confirmation).

9. staf_bbkk's approval is FINAL -- there is no further approval stage anywhere else. The moment they approve, the backend automatically (a) generates the final PDF with the stamp and both signatures, (b) sets the resulting document's type to `phqc` if the transport mode is `kapal`, or `berkas_verifikasi` if `pesawat` (aircraft never receive a PHQC), and (c) sets the submission status to `final`.
10. validator_admin can view and export the resulting documents and data at any time, and manages checklist templates and user accounts, but has no approve/reject action anywhere in their UI.

checklist_system.description: The checklist is never hardcoded per transport mode. It is defined by checklist_templates + checklist_template_items documents, and the mobile form renders fields dynamically based on each item's input_type. This lets BBKK add new transport modes or revise forms through data changes alone, with no app release required. The checklist is filled by kepala_kapal / kepala_penerbangan as a self-declaration, and reviewed by staf_bbkk.

api_endpoints.auth_rule: Every route verifies the caller's Firebase ID token and role via firebase-admin before executing. /submissions/{id}/verify is staf_bbkk only. /users (write) and /checklist-templates (write) are validator_admin only. validator_admin has no access to any approve/reject action anywhere in the API.

security_rules_notes: Firestore rules: kepala_kapal/kepala_penerbangan can only create/read/update their own submissions (pengisi_id == request.auth.uid) while status is `draft`; they cannot edit a submission once it is no longer `draft`.

Firestore rules: staf_bbkk can read submissions with status `menunggu_verifikasi_staf` or `ditolak_otomatis`, and can write only to the verify-related fields (status, verifikator_id) -- enforced primarily through the /verify API route, not direct client writes.

Firestore rules: validator_admin has broad read access for reporting/export. User, checklist, and master-data mutations are performed through audited Admin SDK API routes; client writes to those collections are denied.
Storage rules: evidence media (submission_answer_media) is only writable by the owning pengisi while the submission is in `draft`, and read-accessible to staf_bbkk and validator_admin.
Storage rules: signature images are writable only by the owning user account, and read-only for everyone else (used only server-side when composing PDFs).

security: Role is stored and checked server-side only (custom claims), never trusted from client input.
Firestore and Storage Security Rules enforce role-based read/write access.
The signing PIN is verified server-side on every signing action.
Evidence photos/videos can only be captured via the in-app camera; gallery picking must be disabled for this flow.
Only staf_bbkk can call /submissions/{id}/verify; the backend must reject this call from any other role even if attempted directly.
non_functional_requirements.performance: Compress photo/video client-side before upload. Target <2s response for standard read operations under normal network conditions.
non_functional_requirements.connectivity: The app assumes an active internet connection is available during use. Full offline mode is explicitly out of scope for v1.
non_functional_requirements.scalability: New transport modes or form revisions should be achievable purely through checklist_templates data changes, with no app release required.
non_functional_requirements.auditability: Every submit, approve, reject, document generation, and master-data change writes an audit_log entry.
non_functional_requirements.compatibility: Mobile: Android and iOS from a single Flutter codebase. Web: modern evergreen browsers.

explicitly_out_of_scope_for_v1: QR code / session-code based linking between accounts and inspections
Certified / legally-binding electronic signatures (current signature is a stored image + PIN confirmation only)
Multi-level (cascading) approval workflow -- staf_bbkk's approval is final and single-stage; validator_admin has no approval role at all

glossary.kepala_kapal: Ship captain (Nahkoda). Self-declares the ship's full sanitation form.
glossary.kepala_penerbangan: Pilot / aircraft captain. Self-declares the aircraft's full sanitation form.
glossary.staf_bbkk: BBKK staff who reviews self-declared submissions and gives the final approve/reject decision.
glossary.validator_admin: BBKK staff who administers the system on the web app: users, templates, exports, audit logs. Does not approve/reject submissions.
glossary.ditolak_otomatis: Auto-rejected: the system rejected the submission automatically because at least one checklist item failed. This is informational only for staf_bbkk.
glossary.menunggu_verifikasi_staf: Awaiting staf_bbkk's review, because all checklist items passed automatic evaluation.
glossary.ditolak_staf: staf_bbkk manually rejected the submission after review.
glossary.final: staf_bbkk approved the submission; the resulting document (PHQC or Berkas Verifikasi) has been generated.
glossary.phqc: Port Health Quarantine Clearance -- the official document issued only for approved ship (kapal) submissions.
glossary.berkas_verifikasi: Generic verification document issued for approved aircraft (pesawat) submissions; aircraft never receive a PHQC.
